title: Probability of a dice sum
statement: Roll n fair dice with faces faces (numbered 1..faces). Return the probability that the sum equals target (absolute error ≤ 10⁻⁹).
hints: The distribution of a sum of independent variables is the convolution of their distributions.
dp[s] after k dice; add one die at a time.
complexity: O(n² · faces²) naive, O(n² · faces) with prefix sums

solution.explanation: Sums of independent variables convolve. Adding one die maps dp[s] to Σ_f dp[s − f]/faces, and a sliding window sum makes each step O(n·faces). By the central limit theorem the result is close to normal (mean n(faces + 1)/2, variance n(faces² − 1)/12): useful for estimates in your head. Two dice summing to 7 is 1/6, the single most common quant warm-up.
